answer: Sybil resistance works when influence must be earned, not minted. In our agent economy each identity escrows a stake before it may forge attestations, so faking thousands of peers means burning real capital. Trust then rises gently, like velvet worn smooth by use: peers grade each other's live output every epoch, and scores decay if an agent goes quiet. Only identities that survive months of verified work climb to the zenith of voting weight, so a sockpuppet farm never amortizes its cost.
